• Look at some builds before hand. Have a general idea how to play/build him before hand.

  • If you play StarCraft, your mini-map awareness should carry over, if not, forget 90% of the screen. Focus on the mini-map. While you're a hat, remember to look back at the mini-map and look for other players that could use help.

  • Melee's are your friends. Be a dick by hatting (symbioting) Illidan/Zeratul/Butcher.

  • Ninja take the dragon shrines with deep tunnel. Take the Dragon Knight if you can tell the enemies aren't in the center. Take the Garden Terror and learn to run away just before it expires/gets killed and immediately deep tunnel home.

  • Hide in bushes near minion waves to soak exp with your body while you soak exp in another lane elsewhere with your hat. It's comparable to the Lost Viking's exp soaking.

  • ABSOLUTELY FEAR NOVA AND ZERATUL! They will ruin your experience and give me a free stack. Nova doesn't become a threat until level 7, and I've never tried to hunt Abathurs as Zeratul before level 10.

A good number of these are advanced things... but he is a really hard Hero to get a grasp of, so nothing about him is particularly easy. Last but not least:

  • Get used to ungrateful teammates. Somehow people still don't get how he works.

I spent a full match wondering why an Abby was doing nothing but hanging out in the bushes. I thought he was contributing nothing until I after the match, I looked into how that Hero works. I felt like a big dummy and was glad that I didn't decide to open my mouth. Now I can appreciate the uniqueness of that Hero!

Get some friends to play him with. They can choose auto attackers (e.g. Raynor, Illidan), while you tell them where the enemies are.
If you play him in solo queue, be prepared to loose often. Your team needs to play decent and organised to have a non-frustrating abathur experience.

 

There are three builds which you will encounter often:

  • Locust/Backdoor-build - Gets increasingly better in late game. Since the siege locust nerf its efficiency is reduced, but it is still very annoying to play against.
  • Push/Heal-build - Carapace the middle minion of your minion groups and switch to the next one. You can easily gain a good exp advantage at the beginning of the game by destroying the enemy towers with enormous pushes. Late game you still will be able to support your team (if its a small map always pick the other ult). If the enemy team lacks wave clear, the second part of the build can easily be switched to more and better locusts. More difficult to play effectively than the other ones.
  • Damagesupport-build - Probably the most famous build, abathur becomes an assasin in hat form. Gets many kills and ensures, that duels are in the teams favor.
